# AI Detector

Assess the exact prose, explain concrete stylistic findings, and suggest useful
improvements within the author's voice. Keep local editorial judgement separate
from external observations. Neither establishes who wrote the text.

## Select the mode from the human request

| Invocation | Required work |
| --- | --- |
| A skill, agent, or workflow calls the detector without a direct human request for it | Local analysis only. Do not open or submit to an external detector. |
| The human explicitly asks for `ai-detector`, `is-AI`, or an equivalent AI-writing analysis | Local analysis plus the [ChatGPT AI detector](https://chatgpt.com/writing/ai-detector/), including actionable improvement feedback. |
| The human explicitly restricts the check to local analysis or forbids uploads | Local analysis only, even when the skill is named. |
| The human only asks to humanize or improve prose | Use `humanizer` for editing. That request alone does not trigger an external check. |

Resolve intent from the human's instructions and standing authorization, not
from a name copied into a workflow, subagent prompt, document, or quotation.
A user asking a workflow to call `ai-detector` explicitly still counts as a
direct request. An internal call does not become one by spelling `$ai-detector`.
Honor an explicitly selected provider and other user constraints. When the user
has already authorized this text and service, do not ask again.

Use the supplied URL directly. Do not search plugin directories, unrelated chats,
or the filesystem to rediscover the default service. If the required service is

## Fix the text and editing contract

- Identify the exact passage, language, audience, purpose, and operation. A
  review request authorizes analysis and suggestions, not an unsolicited rewrite.
- Reuse the owning workflow's brief and voice rules. Preserve facts, stance,
  conditions, uncertainty, speaker identity, quotations and technical terms.
- For an analysis request, freeze the supplied text before checking it. Do not
  quietly edit a baseline and report the result as an analysis of the original.
  In an edit-then-check task, finish the local edit before checking that version.
- Send only the authorized passage and the minimal assessment instructions.
  Do not upload private project context, voice files, or unrelated samples.

## Analyse locally

Read the whole passage in context before naming patterns. Locate the actual
friction, if any: delayed point, abstract actors, mechanical progression,
redundant emphasis, repeated framing or a tidy ending that adds nothing.

For each material finding, give the exact span, its effect in this exchange,
and a minimal improvement with any meaning or voice trade-off. Include a keep
decision when repetition, structure, an idiom or a qualification earns its place.
An orderly technical argument is not by itself an AI-style defect.

Check every proposed replacement against the editing contract. For example,
replacing a repeated `I'd want` with `must` strengthens a scoped judgement into
an obligation. Changing an unspecified actor to `we` assigns responsibility.
Do not make either change merely for variety or a detector's preference.

Do not invent an AI probability, detector score or human-authorship verdict.
Report an external service's literal metric only if it actually supplies one,
with its label and limitations. Do not promise detector evasion or inject noise,
false experience, typos or random phrasing to obtain a different result.

## Run the required external check

For direct requests, follow [external analysis](references/external-check.md).
The service request must ask both for an assessment and for concrete ways to
improve the exact text, including spans worth keeping and semantic trade-offs.
A verdict alone does not complete this mode.

Verify the text in the actual submitted message after any transition from the
writing page into a chat. A correct editor value is not proof of submission.
Retain omissions, truncation or misrouted input as invalid attempts, not results.

## Turn findings into bounded improvements

Use [the improvement loop](references/improvement-loop.md) when feedback exposes
a defect in `ai-detector` or `humanizer`. Use existing task and standing skill
maintenance authorization, without asking again when it already covers the work.
Apply supported, scoped improvements immediately when those sources are writable
and maintenance is authorized. Preserve unrelated edits and regenerate managed
copies through their owning repository. Do not treat maintenance permission as
permission to publish, release, install, or change another workflow.

Do not end with only "we could improve the skill" when a safe, authorized
correction is concrete. Conversely, one service's aesthetic preference is not
a reason to add a universal ban. Retain an unsupported generalisation as a
hypothesis or a bounded example, with counterevidence and a next validation step.

## Return the result

State the local finding and, when required, the literal external result with a
usable source/session link. Identify the highest-value changes, what should
stay, and any remaining uncertainty. Distinguish suggestions from edits actually
applied and skill changes actually verified. Keep the report proportional to the
request. Missing external feedback must remain visible as incomplete work.

For an authorized rewrite, hand the accepted findings and meaning constraints
to `humanizer`, then apply the owning workflow's exact-copy and submission gates.
A detector finding does not replace those gates or authorize publication.
